NEW DELHI: The INDIA bloc on Wednesday announced a series of nationwide protests against the Election Commission and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, seeking to project opposition unity amid the ongoing row over voter rolls.Addressing a press conference after the INDIA bloc meeting, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said the alliance would hold district-level “Save Democracy” marches and demonstrations outside district magistrate offices from October 2 to 8.“From October 2 to 8, we will hold district-level 'Save Democracy' marches and stage demonstrations outside the offices of every district magistrate. We will also make people aware of why we are undertaking this campaign,” Kharge said.He said all opposition MPs would march to the Election Commission on October 6. Kharge said the opposition had initially planned to hold the march on Wednesday but decided to organise it later with greater participation.“On October 6, all opposition MPs will march to the Election Commission. We wanted to go today itself, but we decided to call the MPs again and organise the protest properly, so we have fixed October 6 for the march,” he said.Kharge added that Rajya Sabha members and MPs from all parties, as well as those who wanted to “protect democracy in the country”, would be invited to join the march.The alliance also plans to seek an appointment with President Droupadi Murmu in the second week of October. Leaders of the opposition will submit a representation outlining what Kharge described as the difficulties they were facing and the constitutional issues involved.A fourth phase of the campaign will comprise five major rallies, with their dates and venues to be announced later.The INDIA bloc meeting also saw Kharge reiterate his criticism of the Election Commission and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. He alleged that the poll panel was being influenced by the government and said the parties had agreed to fight the issue together.“From October 2 to 8, we will hold district-level 'Save Democracy' marches and stage demonstrations outside the offices of every District Magistrate. We will also make people aware of why we are undertaking this campaign,” Kharge said.Addressing the briefing, ex-Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee lashed out at the CEC and call on him to resign."He (CEC Gyanesh Kumar) must resign immediately. Let us save the democracy and make the security of the people, the voting rights... It is our constitutional rights. It is our obligation to the people. If people are not voting, if their voting are been looted and cheated, then where the country will go? So, our request...it our demand. Our forceful demand," the former Bengal CM said.The opposition has demanded a rollback of the SIR exercise, greater transparency in electoral rolls and safeguards against the exclusion of eligible voters. Kharge also called for the use of pre-SIR electoral rolls for future elections and sought prior notice, reasons and an effective appeal mechanism before legitimate voters are removed.The meeting was attended by representatives of Congress, SP, AITC, NCP(SP), SS (UBT), RJD, CPM, CPI, JKNC, JKPDP, JMM, CPI-ML, IUML, KC(M), MDMK, VCK, RSP, KC(J) and AIFB.
Article Summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said the alliance would hold district- level “Save Democracy” marches and demonstrations outside district magistrate offices from October 2 to 8. He said all opposition MPs would march to the Election Commission on October 6.

Five crew members, including an Indian sailor, were killed by Somali pirates aboard a fuel tanker that was hijacked months ago off the coast of Somalia.Security forces have now regained control of the vessel.According to the Puntland Maritime Police Force (PMPF), the victims also included three Pakistani nationals and one Myanmar national."PMPF carried out a maritime operation off the coast of Dharin-baar, Bandar Beyla District, successfully rescuing the MT Honour 25 oil tanker, which had been hijacked by pirates," it said in a social media post on Tuesday.Puntland is a semi-autonomous region of Somalia.According to the PMPF, the pirates had initially offered to surrender while concealing the deaths of the crew members. It further stated that the ship was now safe and under Puntland government control. Sixteen suspected pirates were apprehended during the operation, while efforts to locate the remaining hijackers were continuing.According to the European Union’s naval force Eunavfor, the MT Honour 25 oil tanker was hijacked in April while sailing towards Somalia’s capital, Mogadishu. It was carrying around 17 crew members, most of them Pakistani nationals, along with a cargo of oil products.BBC Somali reported that the crew comprised 10 Pakistanis, four Indonesians, one Indian, one Sri Lankan and one Myanmar national.The commercial vessel, carrying 18,500 barrels of fuel bound for Mogadishu was hijacked on April 21.In a separate development, Somali pirates on Tuesday released a Togo-flagged tanker after holding it off Puntland’s Karkaar region.Nearly 30 armed pirates disembarked from the vessel and handed over all 12 crew members—eight Egyptians and four Indians—unharmed to the local community. The pirates reportedly damaged the vessel, MT Eureka, and set parts of it on fire before fleeing.The tanker had been hijacked on May 2 off Yemen’s Port of Qana while carrying 20,400 barrels of fuel. A substantial amount of its cargo was siphoned off and sold at sea during the months it was held captive. The crew members are now in the care of local residents in the Hul-Aanood area.
Article Summary: Five crew members, including an Indian sailor, were killed by Somali pirates aboard a fuel tanker that was hijacked months ago off the coast of Somalia. Security forces have now regained control of the vessel. The victims also included three Pakistani nationals and one Myanmar national.

NEW DELHI: A fire that broke out shortly after midnight reduced at least eight houses and several cowsheds to ashes in a remote village in Jammu and Kashmir's Kishtwar district.The fire erupted in a house in Mungli village in the Warwan area and spread rapidly to neighbouring structures. NEW DELHI: Students and members of farmers' and youth organisations staged protests in Bhubaneswar on Wednesday as a 12-hour statewide Odisha bandh was observed over alleged errors in school textbooks and a demand for the resignation of school and mass education minister Nityananda Gond.Members of the Naba Nirman Krushak Sangathan (NNKS) and Nabnirman Yuva Chhatra Sangathan (NYCS) blocked a national highway at Baramunda bus stand and torched tyres during the protest. Accordingly, across Odisha—whether West Odisha, East Odisha, or South Odisha—you will see picketing has started everywhere."The NNKS claimed that more than 1,700 errors had been identified in newly published school textbooks, while NYCS alleged that the number was more than 2,000 in books for Classes 1 to 8. Among the examples cited were a reference to the Niyamgiri Hills as being in Jharkhand and a picture of the Karnataka assembly being used instead of the Odisha assembly. The organisations also alleged that scientist Isaac Newton was described as a pilot.Ali alleged irregularities in the textbook preparation process and claimed corruption worth Rs 380 crore. "Demanding the resignation of Odisha’s Mass Education Minister Nityananda Gond, we have called for an Odisha Bandh today. We request everyone to support this call. In Odisha, for children's school textbooks from Class 1 to Class 8, there are more than 2,000 errors and a corruption of ?380 crore has taken place," he said.The organisations said they had received no response from the government despite their protests. Our organisation’s founder Akshaya Ji has been on protest for 25 days, and today is my 18th day. In Bhubaneswar, police deployed 10 platoons of force and 15 officers at designated locations.

Article Title: Supreme Court imposes 10 lakh cost on UP government for illegal NSA detention
Article Text:
Noting that the action was taken against him almost two months after the incident, despite the probe agency claiming to have video footage, the court said, 'It defies reason as to why it took the agency to arrest the detenu 54 days after registration of the first FIR'.

Confessional statement alone can’t be basis for detention: SC

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh govt failed to give a satisfactory answer for keeping an accused in the 2024 Sambhal violence case under preventive detention for a year under the National Security Act, the Supreme Court said on Tuesday and slapped a Rs 10 lakh fine on the state, to be paid to the detenu. It also reminded the state to "remain faithful" to the preventive detention jurisprudence and not use it as a punitive measure.Declaring the preventive detention, which was resorted to by the state to keep accused Mulla Afroz in custody after he was granted bail, as illegal, a bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu said there were multiple flaws in the decision, as evidence to justify it was insufficient. Mulla's confession before police could not have been the sole ground to invoke preventive detention, as in this case, it said.The reliance placed upon the very same occurrence and substantially the same material for sustaining both criminal and preventive detention proceedings lends considerable force to the contention that the detention order has assumed a character more punitive than preventive. We are, therefore, constrained to observe that the state must remain faithful to the rationale underlying preventive detention jurisprudence," the bench said.The detention order was passed on Oct 13 last year. Granting relief to Mulla, SC said, "The appellant has already suffered considerable loss of liberty, even while being granted bail in all cases related to the incident, in which he featured as an accused. In such circumstances, the process was made a punishment."Noting that the action was taken against him almost two months after the incident, despite the probe agency claiming to have video footage, the court said, “It defies reason as to why it took the agency 54 days to arrest the detenu after registration of the first FIR”.“However, the CCTV footage and video recordings, which appear to constitute the sheet-anchor of the allegation, do not find place among the 22 documents relied upon by the detaining authority. Neither have such recordings been furnished to the appellant nor have they been produced before HC or even before us,” it said. The court said an accused person enjoys the fundamental right against self-incrimination and cannot be compelled to be a witness against himself.“We are of the opinion that a confessional statement made before a police officer cannot, by itself, and in absence of any independent material lending support thereto, constitute a basis for forming the subjective satisfaction necessary to sustain an order of preventive detention,” it said. SC added that to permit this would allow a detention order to rest upon a foundation which the law itself excludes from evidentiary consideration.
Article Summary: Supreme Court slapped a Rs 10 lakh fine on the state, to be paid to the detenu. It also reminded the state to "remain faithful" to the preventive detention jurisprudence and not use it as a punitive measure. The detention order was passed on Oct 13 last year.

NEW DELHI: Ministry of external affairs on Tuesday slammed Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan for raising the Kashmir issue at the United Nations General Assembly and said that no external party has any locus standi on the issue of India's territorial integrity and sovereignty.During a bi-weekly press briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal rejected Erdogan's remarks and said, “You would have seen that the remarks you referred to were made by the Turkey president. India rejects the unwarranted references to India and the Indian Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir made by the President of Turkey during his address to the UN General Assembly.”“This is a matter, as you would understand, pertaining to India’s territorial integrity and sovereignty, and no external party has any locus standi on this issue,” he added.Earlier on September 22, Erdogan had raised the Kashmir issue at UNGA, saying the matter “should be addressed through dialogue.”“In South Asia, it is important that all disputes, including the Kashmir issue, be addressed through dialogue within the framework of the United Nations Charter and of relevant resolutions,” he said.Turkey has raised the Kashmir issue on global platforms in the past as well.Notably, Erdogan-led Turkey has also formed a Nato-like military alliance with two other Islamic nations, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia.The pact, known as the 'Mecca Pact', was signed between the three countries in August this year.India, however, has consistently rejected any third-party mediation in the Kashmir issue and repeatedly maintained that Jammu and Kashmir is an integral part of India.Following the Pakistan-sponsored terror attack in Pahalgam, India made it clear that New Delhi would only engage with Islamabad on Kashmir-related issues bilaterally.
Article Summary: Turkey has raised the Kashmir issue on global platforms in the past as well. Turkey has also formed a Nato-like military alliance with two other Islamic nations, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia. India, however, has consistently rejected any third-party mediation in Kashmir issue.

Every time a brutal rape case shocks the country, the demand returns almost immediately: give the harshest possible punishment.The anger is understandable. But the law applies a much narrower test. Not every rape case, however grave, crosses the threshold for the death penalty.India recorded 29,536 rape cases in 2024, according to the latest National Crime Records Bureau data. In Delhi, 1,058 rape cases were registered that year, while Delhi Police reported 1,901 cases in 2025.The figures come amid renewed attention on sexual violence, with a series of recent cases in Delhi and across the country bringing questions of punishment, deterrence and justice back into focus.While Indian law provides for stringent punishment, including the death penalty in certain rape cases, capital punishment remains restricted to specific circumstances.So when does a rape case cross the legal threshold for the ultimate punishment? What makes one case “rarest of rare”, while another results in life imprisonment?A series of recent cases has once again put women’s safety under scrutiny.In September, a 17-year-old girl was allegedly gang-raped by three men posing as police personnel at Astha Kunj Park near Kalkaji Mandir in Delhi. The case triggered student protests demanding stronger measures for women’s safety, and police arrested the accused.In August, another 17-year-old girl was allegedly gang-raped by a bus driver and conductor after boarding a bus from Greater Noida. She was later dropped near Kashmere Gate. The National Human Rights Commission took suo motu cognisance of the case and sought reports from authorities.Against this backdrop, the Supreme Court on Monday took suo motu cognisance of recent rape incidents in Delhi-NCR, flagging what it described as a "systematic failure" to ensure basic public safety.Concerns have extended beyond Delhi.In Bihar, three incidents involving alleged sexual harassment and assault were reported within days. In Jamui, a teenage boy and girl were allegedly stopped and assaulted by a group of men on September 19, with three accused arrested after a video surfaced online. In Samastipur, a minor girl was allegedly assaulted and molested, while another case in Banka’s Mandar Hill area involved allegations of a woman being harassed and her male friend assaulted.The cases have also spilled onto the streets. Students and young people in the national capital are holding protests demanding safer public spaces, stronger policing and greater accountability.Indian law permits the death penalty in certain aggravated rape cases, including those involving minors and cases where the victim dies or is left in a persistent vegetative state, under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the POCSO Act.But the existence of the death penalty does not mean it follows automatically in the most brutal cases.Advocate Sumit Nagpal said courts consider factors including the brutality of the offence, injuries caused, the vulnerability of the survivor and the long-term consequences while determining punishment.Rupali Jain, who practises in the high court and Supreme Court, said the harm caused by rape, while grave, cannot by itself justify capital punishment."As harm is inherent in every rape, it cannot alone justify death. The court must also apply the 'criminal test', the offender’s age, antecedents, background, custodial conduct and prospects of reform, as reiterated in Manoj v. State of Madhya Pradesh (2022)," she said.The "rarest of rare" doctrine gained renewed attention following the 2012 Nirbhaya case . On December 16, 2012, a 23-year-old woman was gang-raped and brutally assaulted inside a moving bus in Delhi. She died from her injuries days later.Four adult accused were sentenced to death by the trial court in 2013. The Delhi high court upheld the punishment in 2014, and the Supreme Court confirmed the death sentences in 2017, holding that the case fell within the “rarest of rare” category.However, the Supreme Court has also held that the brutality or heinousness of an offence alone does not automatically make it a "rarest of rare" case. Courts must weigh aggravating circumstances against mitigating factors, including the possibility of reform and rehabilitation.But the death penalty is not automatic, even in cases involving extreme violence.The Bilkis Bano case offers another example of how courts apply the 'rarest of rare' test differently.In the Bilkis Bano case, 11 men were convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment for gang rape, murder and other offences linked to the 2002 Gujarat riots. Bilkis was 21 and five months pregnant when she was raped, and several members of her family were killed.The case shows why the "rarest of rare" test is not based only on how brutal or shocking a crime appears. Courts must also consider other factors, including the background of the accused and whether there is any possibility of reform.Activist Yogita Bhayana, however, argues that the impact of rape on the survivor should receive greater weight when courts consider the threshold."Every rape case is rarest of the rare in terms of the victim," she said, arguing that the legal system can focus heavily on physical brutality while overlooking the lasting impact on survivors.Bhayana said she believes the death penalty should remain available in rape cases and argued for greater weight to be given to the consequences of the crime for survivors while deciding punishment.The legal process changes significantly when the accused is under 18.Under the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, a child aged between 16 and 18 who is accused of a “heinous offence”, including rape, can undergo a preliminary assessment by the Juvenile Justice Board.The Board looks at the child’s mental and physical capacity to commit the offence, whether they understood its consequences and the circumstances in which the alleged offence took place.Depending on that assessment, the case can be transferred to the Children’s Court, which then decides whether the child should be tried as an adult.Rupali Jain said the existing law already provides a framework for dealing with serious offences committed by juveniles, and the focus should remain on how it is implemented rather than simply lowering the age threshold.She also pointed out that the Juvenile Justice Act does not allow the death penalty, or life imprisonment without the possibility of release, for a child in conflict with law.However, activist Yogita Bhayana argues that the distinction between different degrees of brutality can be deeply troubling for survivors.“The miner will be treated as miner unless he brutally kills her, rape her in a very gruesome manner. Then otherwise, it will not be in the rarest of the rare category. So we need to change the whole thing,” she said, arguing that the system should focus more closely on the impact of the crime on the survivor and called for greater awareness and stronger mechanisms to deal with sexual offences.For survivors, justice does not necessarily end with an arrest, conviction or sentence.Activist Yogita Bhayana said the distinction between "high-profile" and ordinary rape cases often comes from media attention rather than the nature of the crime or the survivor’s experience."There is no case which is high profile. What becomes media-highlighted becomes high profile," she said, pointing out that even Nirbhaya came from a humble, lower-middle-class family.She said survivors often continue to deal with trauma, repeated questioning and the pressures of the legal process long after public attention has moved on."Attention doesn’t mean justice," Bhayana said.Dr Vinodh Sreeram, senior psychiatrist & addiction specialist at Maarga Mind Care, Bengaluru, said rape can deeply alter a survivor’s sense of safety, relationships and ability to return to everyday life.He cautioned against judging trauma only by visible injuries or by how brutal an assault appears. Two survivors of similar incidents can experience very different psychological effects depending on factors such as age, past experiences, their relationship with the accused and the support available to them."The absence of visible injury should never be mistaken for the absence of psychological trauma," he said.On whether the death penalty can provide psychological closure, Sreeram said there is no single answer. Some survivors or families may see a severe sentence as justice, but "closure rarely comes from the sentence alone".Being believed, treated with dignity, protected from further harm and supported through recovery can be just as important, he said. Repeated questioning, cross-examination, delays and prolonged appeals can themselves become additional sources of distress.Recent protests in Delhi have again brought demands for safer public spaces, stronger policing, better surveillance and greater accountability to the forefront.Advocate Sumit Nagpal said the biggest challenge is not necessarily the absence of laws, but the capacity to enforce them."The bottleneck is capacity, not the statute. India has roughly twenty judges per million people against a recommended fifty, and police strength sits well below sanctioned levels in most states. Until that gap closes, every reform stays on paper," he said."So the real agenda is unglamorous: more investigators, more courts, more forensic capacity, fewer vacancies. No amendment will substitute for that."Activist Yogita Bhayana said the biggest gap remains implementation. While reforms, awareness and gender-sensitisation efforts have increased, she said survivors continue to face inadequate support, delays in fast-track courts and a lack of sensitivity within the system.She also warned that repeated exposure to sexual-violence cases can make institutions become "immune" to such crimes."For them, they see it like an everyday thing," she said, arguing that continued training and sensitisation are needed to ensure sexual violence is not treated as routine.Dr Vinodh Sreeram said debates around harsher punishment must also account for the realities of reporting, particularly because many survivors know the accused and may face fear, stigma and family pressure.A trauma-informed justice system, he said, should focus on sensitive questioning, privacy, timely trials and access to psychological support.“Justice is not only about the severity of punishment. It is also about ensuring that survivors are heard, protected, treated with dignity and given the opportunity to rebuild their lives,” Sreeram said.The death penalty is only one part of the debate. The larger challenge is to prevent such crimes, ensure quicker justice and make sure survivors get the support they need.
Article Summary: India recorded 29,536 rape cases in 2024, according to the latest National Crime Records Bureau data. In Delhi, 1,058 rape cases were registered that year, while Delhi Police reported 1,901 cases in 2025. Figures come amid renewed attention on sexual violence, with a series of recent cases in Delhi and across the country.

Article Title: The Backstory: 10 years of surgical strikes, the 10 days after Uri
Article Text:
How Uri led to surgical strikes (PTI file photo)

ALSO READ:

September 20-22: From anger to options

September 23: The plan takes shape

September 24: PM Modi's warning

India will never forget the sacrifices of our soldiers. PM Modi

September 25-27: Preparing the men

September 28: The night India crossed the LoC

September 29: 'Surgical strikes'

What made 2016 different

From Uri to Balakot

Then came Operation Sindoor

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A decade later: What changed?

NEW DELHI: Ten years ago, on the night of September 28-29, 2016, Indian Army commandos crossed the Line of Control and carried out surgical strikes on terrorist launch pads in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.The operation, carried out in response to the Pakistan-sponsored Uri terror attack, marked a hard-hitting response to Pakistan for sheltering and cultivating terror on its soil.It was the first time India responded not with a traditional full-fledged war, but with a calibrated and deliberate military operation against Islamabad-backed terror infrastructure across the border.It was also a demonstration of the more assertive counter-terrorism approach that the Modi government would later associate with its “New India” and “zero tolerance” messaging.But the story of the surgical strikes did not begin on the night of September 28.It began 10 days earlier, in a burning Army camp in Uri.At around 5.30am on September 18, four heavily armed terrorists attacked the Army's 12th Brigade headquarters in Jammu and Kashmir's Uri, close to the Line of Control.The attack was on a rear administrative camp next to the brigade headquarters.The timing was particularly devastating. Troops were in the middle of a changeover, with an advance party of the incoming 6 Bihar unit in the process of replacing the outgoing 10 Dogra unit.Many soldiers were housed in temporary tents. Explosions and gunfire triggered a fire that spread through the camp.Seventeen soldiers were killed in the initial attack. Two others later succumbed to their injuries, taking the toll to 19.The four attackers were killed then and there.For the families, however, the numbers told only part of the story.In Rajasthan, Havaldar Nimb Singh Rawat's family was preparing to receive his body on what would have been his 48th birthday. A member of 6 Bihar, Rawat had routinely spent his birthdays on duty because his family lived away in Rajsamand district. He left behind his wife, four daughters and a young son.In Samba, 10-year-old Vansh, the son of Havildar Ravi Paul Salotra of 10 Dogra, said he wanted to fulfil his father's dream of becoming an Army doctor.The attack had suddenly turned a distant security crisis into funerals, grieving families and children asking questions.Prime Minister Narendra Modi's first response came within hours.“We strongly condemn the cowardly terror attack in Uri. I assure the nation that those behind this despicable attack will not go unpunished,” PM Modi said.He also said the country saluted those martyred and that their service would always be remembered.The government began examining the attack, including the identity and possible origins of the attackers.Then-home minister Rajnath Singh cancelled a planned visit to Russia and the US and convened a security review in Delhi.“Pakistan is a terrorist state and it should be identified and isolated as such,” Rajnath Singh said on September 18, adding that there were indications that the attackers were highly trained, heavily armed and specially equipped.However, the public anger and government's rhetoric did not immediately translate into military strike.Within 24 hours, the government had begun examining possible responses.National security adviser Ajit Doval chaired a meeting of senior intelligence and military officials, according to contemporary reports, with options being prepared for the Prime Minister.One line attributed to the discussions captured the government's thinking: India would avenge the deaths, but “at a time of our choosing”.Outside the government, the demand for retaliation was growing.BJP general secretary Ram Madhav wrote on Facebook: “For one tooth, the complete jaw.”The expression reflected the anger after Uri. But inside the security establishment, the calculations were more complicated.Pakistan had heightened its alert along the LoC and an immediate strike risked escalation.This was the first crucial decision of the 10-day story.India would respond.But it would decide when, where and how.The government began weighing its choices.Diplomatic pressure was one part of the response. Within hours of the Uri attack, Indian missions abroad were asked to mobilise international condemnation of the attack.Then-external affairs mnister Sushma Swaraj would subsequently use the UN platform to attack Pakistan's support for terrorism.But the military option was also being examined.The Army was already monitoring terrorist infrastructure across the LoC. The DGMO would later say that almost 20 infiltration attempts had been foiled by the Army at or close to the LoC during 2016. India had also recovered GPS devices and other material that it said pointed to Pakistan as the source of the infiltration network.The question was no longer simply whether India could strike.It was whether it could strike in a way that was precise, limited and militarily useful.By the third week of September, the military option was becoming more concrete.The targets were terrorist launch pads close to the LoC, where India believed militants were preparing to infiltrate Jammu and Kashmir.The proposed operation was not conceived as a conventional attack on Pakistan.The intended targets were terrorist infrastructure. The troops would cross the LoC, strike the launch pads and withdraw.The political leadership had to weigh the possibility that Pakistan would retaliate. The military had to work out routes, timings, surveillance and extraction.It was a narrow window between sending a message and triggering something much bigger. There was also a risk of indulging in a war with nuclear-armed neighbour.On September 24, PM Narendra Modi met the chiefs of the Army and Air Force and the vice chief of the Navy, with NSA Ajit Doval also present, as discussions focused on the security situation and India’s response to the Uri attack.Later that day, speaking at a BJP rally in Kerala's Kozhikode, he addressed the families of the soldiers killed in Uri.PM warned that those responsible would be held accountable.The signal was becoming unmistakable. But the military operation remained secret.That evening, there was still no public indication that Indian Special Forces were preparing to cross the LoC.The next few days were quieter in public, but crucial behind the scenes.According to Manohar Parrikar Institute under defence ministry, the Special Forces contingent selected for the operation was divided into smaller groups and moved towards the LoC, close to the Army’s forward positions. Later accounts of the operation said the teams moved after last light, crossed gaps in their own minefields and began closing in on the identified targets.The terrain itself was a challenge. The minefields ahead of Indian defences remained a constant danger, with mines sometimes shifting because of heavy rains and landslides. As the teams moved closer, the target areas were kept under watch for any changes that could affect the mission.At the designated hour, the teams struck.They then began their withdrawal, moving back towards their positions before daybreak.For the soldiers preparing to cross the LoC, this was no longer about speeches in Delhi.It was about moving through difficult terrain in darkness, reaching the targets, completing the mission and making it back safely.The Army would later say the operation was based on “very credible and specific information” about terrorist teams positioned at launch pads along the LoC and preparing to infiltrate and carry out attacks.The political leadership, meanwhile, kept the circle of people aware of the operation tightly controlled.As darkness fell on September 28, the operation entered its final phase.Special Forces teams moved towards their designated targets.In the early hours of September 29, they crossed the Line of Control and entered the areas under Pakistan's illegal occupation where the Army had identified terrorist launch pads.The Army later said the teams struck several launch pads across multiple sectors along the LoC. After completing their mission, they began withdrawing before dawn.The operation was over.Then came the second, equally important decision. India would tell the world what it had done.The announcement came that morning.Then-DGMO Lt Gen Ranbir Singh appeared before the media and said the Army had conducted “surgical strikes” at several launch pads.The decision, he said, followed “very credible and specific information” that terrorist teams had positioned themselves at launch pads along the LoC with the aim of infiltrating Jammu and Kashmir and carrying out terrorist strikes in India.The Army said the strikes had caused “significant casualties” to terrorists and those supporting them.Singh also made clear that the operation had ended, saying there were no plans for further continuation of the strikes.India was not merely signalling that it had retaliated. It was publicly acknowledging that its forces had crossed the LoC and struck what it described as terrorist launch pads.Pakistan rejected India's account of a surgical strike and said its soldiers had come under fire.For the Union government, however, the operation had acquired a significance beyond the battlefield.It had chosen to publicly own the operation and put its account of the events on record.Cross-LoC raids were not unprecedented.Indian troops had conducted tactical operations across the LoC before. What changed in 2016 was the combination of political authorisation, the scale of the operation and, above all, the decision to publicly acknowledge it.The government did not leave the operation as an unconfirmed military action.The then-DGMO briefed the country.The term “surgical strikes” entered India's national-security vocabulary.And the PM Modi-led government presented the operation as a calibrated response to terrorism, rather than the opening move in a conventional war.That distinction was crucial.India had chosen to hit terrorist infrastructure without declaring war on Pakistan.However, the September 2016 strikes did not end Pakistan-manufactured terrorism.In February 2019, a Jaish-e-Mohammed suicide bomber attacked a CRPF convoy in Pulwama, killing 40 personnel.Twelve days later, on February 26, the Indian Air Force carried out an air strike on a Jaish-e-Mohammed facility at Balakot in mainland Pakistan.The response had now moved beyond the LoC as Balakot is close to international border and situated in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.India had demonstrated that air power, too, could be used against terrorist infrastructure across the border.The 2016 template had evolved.In 2025, the response was broader still.Following the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack, which killed 26 people, India launched Operation Sindoor on May 7.The government said the armed forces struck nine terrorist infrastructure sites in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir. It described the initial strikes as "focused and measured".The strikes were not limited to terrorist infrastructure. After Pakistan launched waves of drones and missiles towards Indian territory, New Delhi expanded its response to include military targets.India then struck Pakistani military installations, targeting 11 airbases as part of the broader operation.The confrontation subsequently expanded, involving missiles, drones, air-defence systems and attacks on military targets before the Pakistani side pleaded India for a ceasefire on land, air and water.On Pakistan DGMO's request, India announced ceasefire on May 10.The technology and scale were vastly different from 2016.But the sequence was familiar.The Army's counterterrorism architecture has now evolved.The response now relies heavily on intelligence-led operations, surveillance, drones, satellite imagery, counter-infiltration measures and precision weapons.A decade later, the battlefield is increasingly shaped by sensors, drones, precision weapons and real-time intelligence.
Article Summary: Ten years ago, Indian Army commandos carried out surgical strikes on terrorist launch pads in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir. Operation marked a hard-hitting response to Pakistan for sheltering and cultivating terror on its soil. It was the first time India responded not with a traditional full-fledged war, but with a calibrated and deliberate military operation.

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu minister Aadhav Arjuna launched a sharp attack on the DMK, claiming that the party had underestimated his side and was now in a weak position in the Maduranthakam constituency.Arjuna said the DMK had earlier claimed it would win 200 constituencies but was now sitting in the opposition benches.“The DMK, which said that it would win 200 constituencies, is sitting in the Opposition benches. They took us lightly. They said, ‘These people only know how to blow whistles.’ That very whistle came to us as our symbol, and we have blown them away completely with that whistle,” he said.Arjuna further claimed that the DMK was in a “pathetic position” in the constituency and questioned whether the party would even be able to retain its election deposit.“In this constituency, the DMK is in a pathetic position. Will the DMK even get its deposit back?” he said.He also targeted Tamil Nadu leader of opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin , alleging that his remarks were damaging the DMK.“Everything that comes out of the mouth of Udhayanidhi is only obscenity. No one else needs to come to destroy the DMK; MK Stalin’s son is enough. Udhayanidhi Stalin has come to destroy the DMK,” Arjuna said.Bypolls to the Maduranthakam Assembly constituency in Chengelpet district, adjoining Chennai, and the Dharapuram constituency in Tiruppur district of western Tamil Nadu will be held on October 6.The bypolls were necessitated after AIADMK legislators Maragatham Kumaravel and P Sathyabama resigned from their posts and joined the ruling TVK. The party has fielded both of them from the same constituencies they represented after being elected in the April Assembly election.This is the first time the TVK government is facing Assembly bypolls since it assumed office in May 2026.The Left parties, which extend outside support to the TVK government and help it retain its majority, have not joined the ruling party-led alliance. Instead, they are contesting the bypolls as a separate front.Candidates of the main opposition DMK, the AIADMK and the Tamil nationalist Naam Tamilar Katchi (NTK) are also in the fray.The Vanniyar-dominated PMK, which has considerable influence in several northern parts of the state, has not extended support to any party.A key opposition campaign plank is that the bypolls were not a natural outcome but were forced on voters after the TVK “lured AIADMK MLAs” to strengthen its numbers in the Assembly.AIADMK chief Edappadi K Palaniswami has already begun campaigning, seeking “justice” over what he has described as the betrayal.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu minister Aadhav Arjuna launched a sharp attack on the DMK. He claimed that the party had underestimated his side and was now in a weak position. Bypolls to the Maduranthakam Assembly constituency in Chengelpet district, adjoining Chennai, will be held on October 6.

Article Title: Watch: Landslide blocks Kedarnath route in Rudraprayag’s Chirbasa, over 1,500 pilgrims evacuated

Kedarnath route blocked by landslide in Rudraprayag's Chirbasa village

Pilgrims carefully evacuated from landslide zone

Joint teams complete rescue operation

NEW DELHI: Around 1,500 pilgrims stranded on the Kedarnath route near Chirbasa were safely rescued and escorted to Gaurikund after a landslide blocked the route late Sunday night, officials said.The pilgrims were stranded around three kilometres from Gaurikund after a landslide hit the route near Chirbasa, news agency ANI reported.The Rudraprayag District Control Room (DCR) informed Sonprayag Police about the situation late on September 27, following which the SDRF Sonprayag team, led by Sub-Inspector Ashish Dimri, rushed to the spot.Prioritising the safety of the pilgrims, the rescue teams carefully assisted them across the affected stretch. Around 1,500 pilgrims were brought safely to the other side of the landslide zone and escorted towards Gaurikund.The operation was carried out despite continued rockfall and the risk of further landslides in the area. Rescue personnel coordinated the movement of pilgrims to ensure they crossed the dangerous stretch safely.The coordinated efforts of the SDRF, NDRF and DDRF helped ensure that all the stranded pilgrims were safely evacuated from the affected area.Officials said the rescue operation was successfully completed despite the challenging conditions at the site.
Article Summary: Around 1,500 pilgrims stranded on the Kedarnath route near Chirbasa were safely rescued. The pilgrims were stranded around three kilometres from Gaurikund after a landslide hit the route. Rescue personnel coordinated the movement of pilgrims to ensure they crossed the dangerous stretch.

Article Title: Tensions flare in Ujjain after group clashes with police over portion of Shahi mosque demolition
Article Text:
Heavy police force deployed in the area.

272 structures have been marked for demolition

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think the road-widening project will improve arrangements for the Simhastha Mela? Yes, it will improve accessibility No, it may create challenges 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

(With inputs from ANI)





UJJAIN: A large group of people clashed with police in Ujjain at the spot where a portion of the Shahi Masjid was demolished as part of a road-widening project, news agency ANI reported on Monday.Heavy police force remains deployed in the area.The situation reportedly turned tense when some unidentified individuals began pelting stones in the area. Police personnel intervened to bring the situation under control and fired tear-gas shells to disperse the crowd.The confrontation took place as the Ujjain Municipal Corporation started removing the mosque portion falling within the proposed road alignment for the widening project ahead of Simhastha 2028.Rapid Action Force (RAF) personnel are also present at the spot.Earlier, Madhya Pradesh chief minister Mohan Yadav intitaed various develoment works in Ujjain with the demolition activity carried out at his ancestral home.272 structures have been marked for demolition as part of a road-widening project in Ujjain ahead of the Simhastha 2028 fair.Speaking on the occasion, Yadav said the demolition of his childhood home carried personal significance, but was necessary for the larger cause."This is the place where I grew up, playing and running around, and now I am stepping forward to dismantle it with my own hands. It certainly has an emotional impact. However, if it is necessary for the administration and essential for the Simhastha, then this sacrifice must be made. I am satisfied that we are all doing this together," he said.He added that the gesture was meant to set an example for residents whose properties were also being affected by the project."The entire state and the country are watching this. People are demolishing their homes willingly and happily, dedicating themselves to the cause so that others may benefit greatly," he said.Ujjain Municipal Corporation Chairperson Kalawati Yadav explained the scale of preparations underway for the upcoming religious gathering, as it is one of the biggest spiritual gatherings that happens once every 12 years."In 2028, Ujjain will host the Simhastha Mela, one of the world's largest spiritual gatherings, held every 12 years on the banks of the Shipra River. Extensive preparations are underway, including around 29 kilometres of new ghats, a diversion project, dams and other infrastructure works to improve the city. With millions of devotees expected, road widening has become essential," she said.The road-widening initiative forms part of the broader infrastructure overhaul being undertaken in Ujjain to accommodate the massive influx of pilgrims expected during the Simhastha Mela in 2028.
Article Summary: A large group of people clashed with police in Ujjain at the spot where a portion of the Shahi Masjid was demolished as part of a road-widening project. The situation reportedly turned tense when some unidentified individuals began pelting stones in the area. Police personnel intervened to bring the situation under control and fired tear-gas shells to disperse the crowd.272 structures have been marked for demolition ahead of the Simhastha 2028 fair.

Rape claim, campus unrest and midnight clashes: What happened at LPU

NEW DELHI: Students of Lovely Professional University (LPU) in Punjab’s Phagwara went on a rampage on Sunday, vandalising property and blocking NH-44 during protests over claims that an outsider raped a female student on the university campus. The protests later turned violent as students clashed with police, damaged and set fire to vehicles, and pelted stones at security personnel. Several policemen were injured.The university has suspended regular classes for 10 days from September 28 and postponed mid-term examinations until further notice. Heavy police deployment has been made on the campus, while students have started leaving for their homes.Classes suspended, exams postponedFollowing the violence, LPU suspended regular classes for 10 days from September 28 and postponed mid-term examinations until further notice.The administration appealed to students to remain calm, follow official instructions and stay connected for further updates.Several rounds of talks between protesting students and the university management remained inconclusive.Vice Chancellor Sandhu assured students that their genuine grievances would be addressed.The protesters demanded that LPU Founder-Chancellor Ashok Mittal, who is also a BJP Rajya Sabha MP, visit the protest site and assure them that their concerns would be resolved. They also sought that access to the University Management System not be blocked and that students not be victimised for participating in the protest.A large police force led by ADGP M F Farooqui entered the LPU campus after the violence escalated. More than 2,000 personnel have been deployed to maintain security through the night, Farooqui said.“We will ensure security on the campus throughout the night... A force of over 2,000 personnel is currently deployed here. Law and order has been fully maintained and restored... The process is ongoing, and we are working to keep the situation under control. I cannot provide further details at this moment. To the families whose daughters are staying in the hostel here: please do not worry; everyone is safe... The atmosphere here is completely calm, and the university students are also cooperating with us in restoring peace. ..,” he said.Jalandhar Police Commissioner Satinder Singh said reports of disturbances in the hostels were rumours and that all hostels had been checked.“First of all, reports of disturbances in the hostels were merely rumours. All hostels have been checked, and there are no issues. Traffic has resumed, and the situation is normal. Other matters will be resolved through discussions with the students... Overall, the atmosphere is fine, and any minor issues will be addressed... Please inform the families that all students are safe and there is no cause for concern,” Singh said.DIG (Jalandhar Range) Naveen Singla also said the situation had been brought under control and that traffic movement on NH-44 would soon be restored.Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann has directed strict action against those responsible for the unrest at Lovely Professional University (LPU), the Chief Minister’s Office said.Mann also directed Director General of Police Gaurav Yadav to visit the spot and assess the situation.The protest began near Girls' Hostel-3 around 1 am on Sunday after students alleged that a female student had been raped by a plumber three days earlier. They also claimed the hostel warden had been informed but no action was taken.The protesters blocked NH-44 outside the university from around 8 am, causing long queues of stranded vehicles. Police later attempted to clear the blockade, but students allegedly threw water bottles at them and clashed with personnel.Police resorted to a mild lathi charge, following which students moved towards the campus and continued to pelt stones at police vehicles. Two police vehicles were set on fire, while four to five vehicles were damaged, according to Jalandhar Rural SSP Harvinder Singh Virk.Viral videos showed damaged property, vehicles and an ATM kiosk on the campus. Some students were also seen climbing onto a decommissioned MiG-23UM aircraft and a military tank installed on the premises.A truck driver, Vikas Yadav, said, “We have been stranded since 7 AM; there is no sign of things opening up yet... We are extremely distressed... We have had to abandon our vehicles and flee...”Police said an FIR had been registered against an unknown person based on a complaint by the students and a special investigation team had been formed.Singla said the girl was staying in Hostel No. 3 and had returned to her home after students alleged that no action had been taken on the matter. He said the investigation would involve student representatives.“We will analyse forensic samples, CCTV camera footage, call records, etc., before reaching a conclusion,” Singla said.The DIG also said students had demanded that the hostel staff comprise only women, adding that the management would address the demand.Asked about another death, Singla said a female student from Telangana studying at LPU had died by suicide 15 days earlier. “If the students say that there was foul play, action will be taken,” he said.LPU Vice Chancellor Jaspal Singh Sandhu said the university was not aware of any such rape incident but would cooperate with the investigation.LPU management has denied the rape allegations, with Registrar Monica Gulati saying certain “anti-social elements” were spreading “false, baseless and fabricated” claims.The university released a video featuring three female students identified as residents of Room No. 504 of the hostel. In the video, the students said no rape had taken place in their room and asked police and other students not to disturb them.Gulati introduced the video by saying, “I would like you to hear what the girls residing in room number 504 of GH3 told us.”The first student said, “So, we are the residents of room number 504. Nothing of that sort happened in our room; we have been living here for the past two months. Please, police and students, do not bother us. Nothing like that happened in our room, and we are not involved in this at all.”The second student said, “We have been extremely distressed today, and if we face further trouble, we will involve our parents. Please do not harass us.”The third added, “And the police should also stop coming to our room repeatedly; otherwise, we will call our parents.”Gulati later said, “The only conclusion to be drawn from all this is that anti-social elements and individuals with vested interests are behind this.”The opposition Congress criticised the AAP government over the law and order situation in Punjab.“What is happening at LPU is deeply concerning. If students have serious questions or concerns about any incident, they deserve transparent, impartial and time-bound answers, not rumours or suppression. The violence is a testament to the failed law and order situation in Punjab,” state Congress chief Amrinder Singh Raja Warring said.“NH-44 has been blocked since the morning, yet not a single representative from the AAP government has bothered to meet the students and hear their grievances,” Warring said.
Article Summary: Students of Lovely Professional University (LPU) in Punjab’s Phagwara went on a rampage on Sunday, vandalising property and blocking NH-44 during protests over claims that an outsider raped a female student. The protests later turned violent as students clashed with police, damaged and set fire to vehicles, and pelted stones at security personnel. More than 2,000 personnel have been deployed to maintain security through the night.

Article Title: Hijacking scare on Dubai-Tel Aviv flight; emergency code triggered, plane diverted to Saudi Arabia
Article Text:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu held consultations with security officials after the flight was diverted

Netanyahu, military officials hold consultations

A Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv carrying around 180 people landed at Tabuk airport in Saudi Arabia on Wednesday after transmitting emergency signals that triggered a reported hijack scare.The aircraft initially transmitted squawk code 7700, the international transponder code for a general emergency, before sending code 7500, which indicates hijacking or unlawful interference, according to flight-tracking data cited by The Times of Israel. The aircraft subsequently turned around while flying over Saudi Arabia and was diverted to Tabuk, where it landed safely.The incident that prompted the emergency signals was apparently an altercation between the pilots aboard the aircraft, according to Israeli security sources cited by The Times of Israel. The report said a hijacking was subsequently ruled out.The 7500 signal prompted Israeli Air Force fighter jets to scramble towards the aircraft, according to Israeli security sources cited by the publication. The aircraft also briefly disappeared from flight-tracking websites after transmitting the emergency signals, adding to the uncertainty surrounding the incident.Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu held consultations with security officials after the flight was diverted, three Israeli security officials told Reuters.An Israeli source had earlier said the situation would become clearer once the aircraft landed in Saudi Arabia.The Israel Defence Forces also held an assessment of the incident. IDF Chief of Staff Lt Gen Eyal Zamir met senior officers including Israeli Air Force chief Maj Gen Omer Tischler, Operations Directorate chief Maj Gen Itzik Cohen and Intelligence Directorate chief Maj Gen Shlomi Binder, The Times of Israel reported.
Article Summary: Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv carrying around 180 people landed at Tabuk airport in Saudi Arabia on Wednesday after transmitting emergency signals. The aircraft initially transmitted squawk code 7700, the international transponder code for a general emergency, before sending code 7500, which indicates hijacking or unlawful interference. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu held consultations with security officials after the flight was diverted.

Article Title: Auto driver held for abusing, assaulting women in Bengaluru
Article Text:
The driver, who reached the location, abused her and when she retorted, he assaulted her and her friend, a senior police officer said.





BENGALURU: A day after the video of a fight between an autorickshaw driver and two women in HSR Layout went viral, police arrested 30-year-old driver Chetan One of the women, in her 20s, went to the police station Tuesday and filed a complaint after cops got in touch with her.The woman told police she had booked the auto through an aggregator app and subsequently cancelled it.The driver, who reached the location, abused her and when she retorted, he assaulted her and her friend, a senior police officer said.A case has been registered under Section 74 (assault or use of criminal force to a woman with intent to outrage her modesty).The video of them fighting and exchanging blows went viral on social media Monday. GAYA: Two people have been arrested after a minor boy and girl were allegedly abused and assaulted by a group of youths near a hill in Mahuadih village under Sherghati police station on Monday.Police action followed after a video purportedly showing the incident surfaced on social media.According to police, the boy and girl were travelling on a motorcycle when they reached the area and were allegedly stopped by a group of youths. Article Title: Meerut mosque fortified after Hindu outfit announces puja in it
Article Text:

TOI





MEERUT: Heavy police force was deployed around a mosque in Meerut’s Kesarganj area on Tuesday after a Hindu outfit announced plans to recite Hanuman Chalisa at the site, escalating tensions amid an ongoing dispute over construction at the mosque.Police cordoned off the area, stepped up identity checks and began monitoring social media, warning that no one would be allowed to disturb peace or take law into their own hands.The security deployment followed circulation of a video on Monday in which Hindu Raksha Dal announced that its members would recite Hanuman Chalisa outside the mosque.Mosque mutawalli Mohd Zubair approached SSP’s office with a complaint later that night, while local leader Rashid Akhlaq separately submitted a police complaint.SP (city) Vinayak Gopal Bhosle said additional personnel had been deployed considering the sensitivity of the situation and police were keeping watch on both the site and online activity. The Muslim side, which described the mosque as a historical heritage structure, also sought action against those making allegations about it.The confrontation followed a dispute over construction at and around the mosque. Traders led by Meerut Merchants Association president Naveen Bansal had questioned whether requisite permissions had been obtained and protested against the work, following which police stopped the construction.On Sept 12, the association sought an inquiry into the matter.Badar Ali, representing the Muslim community, said construction had been under way on the first floor of the centuries-old mosque but its committee agreed to halt the work after police intervened. “After the controversy erupted, police requested the mosque committee to stop the construction, which was agreed upon. However, a few outside elements made comments on social media that led to tension here. We have appealed to both communities to maintain calm,” Ali told

Article Title: Video: BMC worker killed, 2 injured after ex-MP’s speeding car hits scooters in Mumbai
Article Text:
A tragic incident occurred in Khar West when a speeding car collided with two scooters.





MUMBAI: A BMC employee was killed and two others injured after a speeding car allegedly rammed into two scooters on CD Road in Khar West on Monday, with CCTV footage capturing the crash.Police have registered an FIR against retired honorary Brigadier and former Rajapur MP Sudhir Sawant in connection with the incident.The CCTV footage shows the car hitting the scooters on the busy road, after which Iyappan Harijan, 41, was trapped underneath the vehicle. Bystanders lifted the car and pulled him out before he and his wife Nancy, 37, were taken to Bhabha Hospital in an autorickshaw.Harijan suffered severe injuries and repeatedly lost consciousness while being taken to hospital. He later died from blood loss.Nancy, who was riding pillion, suffered bruises on her left hand and other parts of her body. Another scooter rider, Rahul Ghanekar, suffered a fractured hand.Recalling the crash, Nancy said she saw her husband trapped beneath the car, with only his leg visible. People gathered at the spot and lifted the vehicle to pull him out. She said Harijan initially managed to sit up but had injuries to his head, face and other parts of his body.Khar police on Tuesday registered an FIR against Sawant, 71, under relevant Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita sections for causing death by negligence and rash and dangerous driving.Police said further action would be taken after Sawant is discharged from hospital. He was undergoing treatment after his blood pressure rose following the accident.According to Nancy’s complaint, the couple had left their home in Santacruz West around 4.15pm to shop in Bandra for an event at their home when the car allegedly hit their scooter from behind.Harijan had worked with MTNL for 16 years before joining BMC’s cleaning services department about a month ago. Sawant, a former Rajapur MP, remained active in party politics until late 2019.
Article Summary: A BMC employee was killed and two others injured after a speeding car allegedly rammed into two scooters on CD Road in Khar West on Monday. Police have registered an FIR against retired honorary Brigadier and former Rajapur MP Sudhir Sawant in connection with the incident.

Article Title: Jamia Millia Islamia suspends PhD scholar for 5 days over protest against hostel evictions
Article Text:
The notice said his actions amounted to “gross misconduct” under various clauses of the university’s students’ discipline ordinance.





NEW DELHI: Jamia Millia Islamia has suspended a PhD scholar for five days for allegedly participating in a protest gathering on Monday against the alleged “retaliatory” eviction notices served to several women hostellers who had staged a prolonged agitation over bugs found in mess food. The scholar has been barred from entering the campus during the suspension period.The show-cause notice, issued by the office of the chief proctor on Sept 28, said an unauthorised gathering was held at the central canteen at 5pm that day, disrupting the university’s routine functioning and affecting teaching, learning and research activities in nearby departments, laboratories and libraries. It accused the scholar of delivering a speech and “giving publicity to misleading accounts and rumours”, thereby inciting other students to breach discipline.The notice said his actions amounted to “gross misconduct” under various clauses of the university’s students’ discipline ordinance. He has been directed to explain by Oct 5 why a higher punishment should not be imposed.Speaking to TOI, the student said the protest was organised by women hostel residents against a recent alleged forced eviction, which they believed was retaliatory following their protests over food safety in the mess.Earlier, hostellers had alleged eviction notices were served on them for participating in protests against the mess food. The administration, however, had said the students did not meet the eligibility criteria and that hostel renewal was carried out every year on the basis of merit.Saima Saeed, chief public relations officer, Jamia Millia Islamia, said the university is not stopping anyone from exercising their right to protest. “The university has a designated site for protests, as per court orders, and if anyone violates these guidelines and disrupts the academic environment, the university is bound to take action. Secondly, Jamia follows a merit-based hostel allocation system. If a student does not meet the prescribed 55% marks criterion, we are only following the established procedure. There is no correlation between the mess food protest and the eviction notices,” Saeed said.
Article Summary: The show-cause notice, issued by the office of the chief proctor on Sept 28, said an unauthorised gathering was held at the central canteen at 5pm that day. It accused the scholar of delivering a speech and “giving publicity to misleading accounts and rumours’ The notice said his actions amounted to “gross misconduct” under various clauses of the university’s students’ discipline ordinance.

Article Title: Retired IAS officer found dead with throat slit at Bhopal home; caretaker missing
Article Text:
Ratibad police, senior officers and forensic experts reached the spot and began investigating the death.





BHOPAL: A retired IAS officer, Rakesh Agrawal, was allegedly found dead with his throat slit at his residence behind Panghat Colony in Suraj Nagar in Ratibad early Wednesday morning.A caretaker, who had reportedly been hired through an agency just four days ago, was found missing from the house.Police suspect the caretaker may have fled after the incident. His belongings, except for a pair of clothes, were reportedly missing from the premises. He is said to be from Punjab.According to preliminary information, Agrawal and his wife slept in separate rooms. Around 4am, his wife woke up and found the door of her room latched from outside.She called another caretaker, Amar, who stayed in the servant quarters. Amar opened the door, following which they checked Agrawal's room and found that it too had been latched from outside.When the door was opened, Agrawal was found lying dead inside. His throat had allegedly been slit.Teams from Ratibad police station, along with senior police officers and forensic experts, reached the spot and began investigating the circumstances surrounding the death.The forensic team examined the scene and collected evidence.Senior IAS officers also reached the residence after learning about the incident. Police are investigating the missing caretaker's whereabouts and examining the circumstances leading up to Agrawal's death.ACP Ankita Khatarkar said retired IAS officer Rakesh Agrawal had been discharged from hospital around 20 days ago after treatment for a slip disc-related condition.Police identified the absconding caretaker as Varun Kumar, who had been hired through an agency three days ago as a 24-hour caretaker-cum-male nurse. Kumar is currently untraceable, and police suspect he may have fled after the incident.According to ACP Khatarkar, some almirahs at the house were found open, indicating that robbery could be a possible motive behind the murder. Police are examining the scene and other evidence to establish the sequence of events.The nozzles of LPG cylinders in the kitchen were also found open. Police suspect the cylinders may have been deliberately left leaking, possibly in an attempt to trigger a fire at the house.Agrawal's son is currently in the US. The house did not have CCTV cameras installed, prompting police teams to scan footage from cameras installed in the surrounding area to establish the suspected accused's exit route and trace his movements.Investigators are continuing efforts to locate Kumar and ascertain the circumstances surrounding Agrawal's death.The murder time is suspected to be between 2am and 3am.
Article Summary: Rakesh Agrawal, a retired IAS officer, was allegedly found dead with his throat slit at his residence behind Panghat Colony in Suraj Nagar in Ratibad early Wednesday morning. A caretaker, who had reportedly been hired through an agency just four days ago, was found missing from the house.

Article Title: ‘UP is my karmabhoomi, state will be starting point of my political journey’: Ex-IAS Divya Mittal
Article Text:
In a video statement, Mittal said her administrative experience drove her decision.





LUCKNOW: Former IAS officer Divya Mittal on Tuesday announced her entry into politics but said she won’t join any party. Uttar Pradesh is my “karmabhoomi” and the state would be the starting point of my political journey, she said.Mittal, a 2013 batch UP cadre officer, resigned from the service earlier this month. Mittal said she would work directly with citizens and build an independent platform.She alleged that rumours circulated after her resignation were intended to discourage newcomers from entering public life. “I will not be deterred from raising public issues,” she said.In a video statement, Mittal said her administrative experience drove her decision. “I realised that many problems of the public do not get resolved even when approvals, funds and provisions are in place,” she said, adding, “There are people whose voices do not reach govt, and even when they do, their problems remain unheard.”“I want politics of intent, justice, concern and long-term thinking,” she said. “My objective is not just to replace political leaders. It is to change the way politics functions,” she added.She cited the example of a remote village where residents had sought a school offering education beyond Class V. Mittal said she approved the proposal, but construction had not begun years later. “It was not a question of funds or rules. There was a lack of intent,” she said.She also referred to a landless beneficiary who had official documents for an allotted plot but did not get its physical possession. “Inquiries found irregularities in the reports, and corrective action was taken. Yet the work did not move forward,” Mittal said, questioning what she described as “higher-level interference” in cases where people were legally entitled to relief.Mittal said she wanted to take up issues, including poor rural infrastructure, unsafe roads, examination paper leaks and employment concerns in the age of artificial intelligence. These, she said, needed greater public debate and attention from policymakers.She appealed to people from different walks of life, including teachers, farmers, students, doctors, labourers and lawyers, to join her effort. “Meaningful political change can come only through collective public participation,” she said.During her 13-year career, she also served as the district magistrate of Mirzapur and Deoria.
Article Summary: Mittal, a 2013 batch UP cadre officer, resigned from the service earlier this month. Mittal said she would work directly with citizens and build an independent platform. She alleged that rumours circulated after her resignation were intended to discourage newcomers from entering public life.

Article Title: Puja Khedkar’s parents booked for disproportionate assets
Article Text:

TOI





NASHIK: Anti-Corruption Bureau, Nashik Range, has booked retired Maharashtra Pollution Control Board regional officer Dilip Kondiba Khedkar and his wife Manorama after an inquiry allegedly found that he had accumulated assets 102% beyond his known sources of income during his service.A case has been registered against the couple at the Pathardi police station under relevant provisions of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, and Indian Penal Code.“An open inquiry by the ACB revealed that during his service tenure, Dilip Khedkar acquired disproportionate assets amounting to 102% beyond his known sources of income,” investigating officer and ACB deputy SP Ajit Tripute said.ACB has named Manorama as a co-accused, alleging that she helped her husband accumulate the disproportionate assets. “There is no immediate need to arrest the couple. They will be called for inquiry from time to time,” Tripute said.Explaining the investigation, Tripute said the ACB first undertakes a discreet inquiry after receiving a complaint seeking a probe into a public servant’s wealth. “If officials find grounds for further investigation, permission is obtained from govt to conduct an open inquiry,” he said. The alleged disproportionate assets were detected during this open inquiry.repeatedly tried to contact Khedkar on Tuesday for his response. His phone was switched off. A message was also sent to him, but no response was received till late at night.(with inputs from Gitesh Shelke in Pune)
Article Summary: Anti-Corruption Bureau, Nashik Range, has booked retired Maharashtra Pollution Control Board regional officer Dilip Kondiba Khedkar and his wife Manorama. ACB has named Manorama as a co-accused, alleging that she helped her husband accumulate the disproportionate assets.

Article Title: Smita Thackeray performs 'pind daan','shraddh' for Balasaheb Thackeray in Bihar's Gaya
