Article Title: Antilia bomb scare case: HC bench recuses in NIA's appeal against bail granted to Sachin Waze
Article Text:
The NIA had alleged that Sachin Waze intended to create fear in the Ambani family, possibly to extort money.





MUMBAI: Following two recusals, a third division bench of Bombay HC comprising Justices Girish Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale on Wednesday stayed the bail granted by a special NIA court to former police officer Sachin Waze in the five year old Antilia bomb scare and Mansukh Hiran murder case under the anti-terror law—UAPA.The Justice Kulkarni-led bench issued notice to Waze and posted the matter for hearing on October 7.When the matter originally came up on Wednesday as scheduled and listed before a division bench of Justices Bharti Dangre and Ashish Chavan, Justice Dangre asked if Waze was released or not as yet. Additional Solicitor General Anil Singh for NIA said Waze was not released. Justices Bharati Dangre and Ashish Chavan recused themselves from hearing an appeal filed by National Investigation Agency (NIA) to the bail that special trial court granted on Tuesday to dismissed police officer Sachin Waze in the five year old Antilia bomb scare and Mansukh Hiran murder case under the anti-terror law—UAPA.Waze has spent 1,999 days in custody.Justice Dangre then said she had earlier passed a reasoned order in a matter where “this very person’ (Waze) was a co-accused along with a former minister. The ASG said this was not a connected matter. Justice Dangre said she had earlier already --in September 2024--recused and directed that Waze’s matter in the NIA case not be placed before a bench where she is a party. Her 2024 order was in a plea filed by Waze to quash the proceedings against him.Justice Dangre said to the ASG, “We understand and appreciate your inconvenience’’ and expressed regret that the matter would now have to be placed before another bench.Justice Chavan—who was appointed as Judge last year--too recused saying he had as a lawyer appeared for the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) in a distinctly connected matter.On Tuesday, HC division bench of Justices Sarang Kotwal and RR Bhonsale had recused itself when the ASG had mentioned the challenge and sought urgent hearing.After Justice Dangre and Justice Chavan recused in the morning, the ASG Singh representing NIA, mentioned the matter before the HC Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi to have it assigned before another bench. He said the reason he sought the CJ's intervention was since three other division benches had a Judge who had been appearing for the Central government and were representing its agencies in the case when they were lawyers. The CJ assigned the mater to Justice Kulkarni's bench, before who the NIA then went and sought a stay on Waze's release from Thane Central prison.On Feb 25, 2021, an explosives-laden SUV was found near Antilia in south Mumbai. The NIA alleged that Waze orchestrated the plot to extort wealthy individuals and project himself as a “super cop” after returning to the police force from a long suspension. According to the agency, Waze used a Scorpio owned by Mansukh Hiran, fabricated theft proceedings, and planted gelatin sticks and a threat note in the vehicle. Hiran was allegedly murdered on March 4, 2021, because he knew of the conspiracy and could expose it. Waze was arrested later that month.On Tuesday, special NIA court judge Chakor S Baviskar granting bail to Waze had held that there was “absolutely nothing on record” to infer that industrialist Mukesh Ambani or his family were ever terrorized.The NIA had alleged that Waze intended to create fear in the Ambani family, possibly to extort money. The court called this “quite hypothetical”, saying there was “literally no iota of material” to show any demand for money by Waze from the Ambanis.The judge observed that the SUV containing gelatin sticks was parked near Shikharkunj building on Carmichael Road, and not directly opposite Antilia on Altamount Road. It said the distance between the two spots was considerable, with several buildings in between. “Hence, even the threat to the alleged target does not carry that much weight so as to create terror in their or anyone’s mind,” the judge said.The court observed that the day-to-day business of the Ambanis did not appear to have been disturbed “even for a minute” after the incident. The court said there was nothing to show whether any member of the family even came to know that an explosives-laden vehicle had been parked near their residence. It also pointed out that no member of the Ambani family had lodged a complaint or given a statement during the investigation.Questioning NIA’s probe, the trial court said, “No one knows which Muhurat the investigating agency is waiting for to record statements of any of the targets of the alleged terror, after such a long gap of 5-6 years,” the court said. It added that the failure to record statements of the alleged targets was “precarious to the credibility of the prosecution case”.The NIA office is “literally just wall to wall adjacent” to Antilia the trial Judge said adding “this lassitude has to be seen with great pity and compassion”.In its appeal against the bail, NIA before the HC said the bail order was “eeroneous and ilegal’’ passed without going into detailed facts and circumstances and is “completely misplaced both, on facts and law.’’The NIA says, the special NIA court “completely ignored the rigours of section 43 D of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act while granting bail to the main accused (Waze) whose role is ‘central’ in character to the terror crime of this case.’’The NIA in its appeal said the “very substratum of the prosecution case is that, Waze after his reinstatement in police service after a long suspension, wanted to regain his clout’’ More over he was under the compelling circumstances to collect Rs 100 crore per month from hoteliers and bar owners in Mumbai and territory, and in that process, he intended huge monetary gain for himself also and for that hatched a criminal conspiracy with other accused in this case and committed all the alleged offences. ’’
Article Summary: HC stays the bail granted by a special NIA court to former police officer Sachin Waze in the five year old Antilia bomb scare and Mansukh Hiran murder case under the anti-terror law. Justices Bharati Dangre and Ashish Chavan recused themselves from hearing an appeal filed by National Investigation Agency (NIA) to the bail.

Article Title: DU graduate from Assam, 20 days into Delhi internship, killed as DTC bus hits her Uber bike taxi
Article Text:
Hrishita Lahon, a 22-year-old master's student, died following a road accident near Ashram Flyover.





NEW DELHI: A 22-year-old sociology student of IGNOU, who had joined an internship programme around 20 days ago, died after the Uber bike taxi she was travelling on was allegedly hit by a DTC bus near Ashram Flyover on Monday.The deceased was identified as Hrishita Lahon, a graduate of Maitreyi College, University of Delhi. She was pursuing a master’s degree in sociology from IGNOU and had moved to Delhi for her higher studies and internship.Lahon was travelling from Lajpat Nagar towards Noida when the accident took place around 10am. Police said no PCR call was received from the spot and they first learnt about the accident through a medico-legal case (MLC) received from a hospital around 12.58pm.According to police, the MLC stated that Lahon had suffered injuries in a road accident involving a DTC bus near Ashram Flyover. She was later shifted to another hospital in Sarita Vihar as her condition was critical. She succumbed to her injuries around 2.05pm. Her statement could not be recorded.The bike taxi was being ridden by Darab Singh, who was also injured in the crash. During preliminary inquiry, Singh told police that a bus had allegedly hit the motorcycle from behind.He received treatment at a hospital but left before his statement could be formally recorded and later travelled to Haryana for further treatment.Police searched the area around Ashram Flyover and tried to identify eyewitnesses but could not find anyone who had seen the accident. The motorcycle is also being examined as part of the investigation.A case has been registered at Sunlight Colony police station under Sections 281 (rash driving), 106(1) (causing death by negligence) and 125(A) (act endangering life or personal safety of others) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.Lahon’s postmortem was conducted at AIIMS, following which her body was handed over to her family. Police said further investigation is underway.
Article Summary: The deceased was identified as Hrishita Lahon, a graduate of Maitreyi College, University of Delhi. She was pursuing a master’s degree in sociology from IGNOU. Lahon was travelling from Lajpat Nagar towards Noida when the accident took place.

Article Title: Fort Kochi’s 300-year-old Koder House completely gutted in fire
Article Text:
Koder House, a significant heritage structure in Fort Kochi, suffered complete destruction due to a fire.

Koder House’s Jewish connection

300-year-old heritage landmark destroyed





KOCHI: The historic Koder House in Fort Kochi, a 300-year-old landmark associated with the city’s Jewish heritage, was completely damaged in a fire on Tuesday, raising concerns over the loss of one of the area’s best-known heritage structures.The building, located on Tower Road, was associated with the Koder family, one of the prominent Jewish business families of Kochi.Samuel Koder, a Jewish leader and businessman, was associated with the property. The building dates back to the 1800s and is known for its Portuguese-style architecture.Koder House was associated with the Koder family, which was prominent in Kochi’s Jewish community.Samuel Koder was an influential member of the community and was involved in several businesses in the city.The historic structure, known for its heritage architecture, was completely damaged in the fire.The property had later been used as a heritage boutique hotel and had also hosted Jewish cultural events.The fire has now brought renewed attention to the preservation of Fort Kochi’s historic buildings and the loss of one of the area’s prominent heritage landmarks.
Article Summary: Koder House was associated with the Koder family, one of the prominent Jewish business families of Kochi. The building dates back to the 1800s and is known for its Portuguese-style architecture. The property had later been used as a heritage boutique hotel and had also hosted Jewish cultural events.

Article Title: Hyderabad woman Sandhya Reddy becomes mayor of Sydney council
Article Text:
Sandhya Reddy, originally from Hyderabad, has become the mayor of Strathfield Council in Sydney





HYDERABAD: A Hyderabad-origin woman, Sandhya Reddy, was elected mayor of Strathfield Council in Sydney, Australia, on Tuesday. According to members of the migrant community, she is the first Indian-born migrant woman to serve as a mayor in Australia.Affectionately known as Sandy, Reddy began her journey with the State Emergency Service in 2014 and was elected to the Strathfield Council as an independent councillor in 2021. In 2023, she was elected deputy mayor of the council.A lawyer by profession, Reddy was born and raised in Hyderabad, where she also pursued her education before moving to Australia in 2005. She has been living in the country ever since.Members of the Indian community in Australia hailed her achievement, describing it as both "symbolic and significant" for the country's multicultural communities.
Article Summary: Sandhya Reddy, originally from Hyderabad, has become the mayor of Strathfield Council in Sydney. She is the first Indian-born migrant woman to serve as a mayor in Australia. Reddy began her journey with the State Emergency Service in 2014.

Article Title: Jaipur man held for killing pregnant live-in partner, burying body in rented house courtyard
Article Text:
The murder came to light on Sept 27, (Representative Image)





JAIPUR: Police here Tuesday arrested a 20-year-old man for allegedly strangling his pregnant live-in partner and burying her body in the courtyard of their rented house in Prestige Garden Colony, Bindayaka.DCP (West) Prashant Kiran identified the accused as Pravesh Kumar alias Haggu. Police said he allegedly killed Kiran Rawat on Sept 23 after suspecting her of having an affair with another man. The two were related as nephew and aunt and had been living together as partners.The murder came to light on Sept 27 when the house owner found Kiran’s body buried in the courtyard. Police said Kumar had poured about two kilograms of salt over the body before digging a pit and burying her.During questioning, Kumar told police that he strangled Kiran with one hand and covered her nose and mouth with a cloth with the other. He initially tried to mislead investigators by claiming that Kiran had died by suicide and that he buried her body after panicking, police said.Kumar and Kiran had come to Jaipur from their village about two months ago. Kiran was pregnant and Kumar was living with her and taking care of her.The two used the same mobile phone. Kumar worked odd jobs to support them, police said.After the murder, Kumar allegedly switched off the phone and went to Samod on foot to visit the Hanuman temple.Police said he told them he went there to “wash away his sins”. He returned to work and stayed there from Sept 24 to 26.On Sept 27, after suspecting that the murder had been discovered, Kumar allegedly collected Rs 500 in wages from the factory owner and fled Jaipur.Police teams began searching for him after recovering Kiran’s body. Investigators examined CCTV footage, analysed technical evidence and prepared a route chart to track his movements.A police team eventually detained him on Agra-Lucknow Expressway and arrested him after questioning.Kumar is a resident of Parsa Auliya Lalpur village under Safdarganj police station in Barabanki, Uttar Pradesh.
Article Summary: Pravesh Kumar allegedly killed Kiran Rawat on Sept 23 after suspecting her of having an affair with another man. The two were related as nephew and aunt and had been living together as partners. Police said Kumar had poured about two kilograms of salt over the body before digging a pit and burying her.

A loud explosion-like sound was reported from the Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd premises on Wednesday.

MANGALURU: A blast followed by a fire was reported at the CHT unit, the Hydro Sulphur Treatment Unit of Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd (MRPL), on Wednesday.The fire has since been brought under control, city police commissioner Sudheer Kumar Reddy CH said.One person, identified as Rajesh Baptist, sustained burn injuries covering around 35% of his body and was shifted to Srinivasa Hospital. He is undergoing treatment in the ICU and doctors said he is out of danger.Six other people who suffered minor injuries at an adjacent office were given outpatient treatment and underwent medical check-ups, police said.The city police commissioner, deputy commissioner and Zilla Panchayat CEO are present at the site. Police said there was no major cause for concern and that necessary precautionary measures were being taken.MRPL also confirmed that there were no casualties in the incident and appealed to people not to panic.The blast sent a loud boom across several kilometres, with thick black smoke billowing from the refinery premises. Residents of Jokatte and Surathkal reported that their houses shook and doors and windows vibrated following the explosion.The blast was also reportedly heard at Mangaluru airport, where windows of the administrative office rattled. Fire tenders and emergency teams were rushed to the refinery, while ambulances were seen leaving the premises.On the advice of the district administration, Mangaluru airport is conducting a visual inspection of vital installations in and around the airport, including the Precision Approach Lighting Category I systems and peripheral roads, to check their operational readiness.Dakshina Kannada MP Capt Brijesh Chowta said he was in constant touch with MRPL officials, the police commissioner and Fire and Emergency Services Department officials and was proceeding to the spot to assess the situation.He appealed to people to remain calm, refrain from spreading rumours or misinformation, and cooperate with the administration. Local hospitals were also instructed to remain prepared as a precautionary measure.

One person sustained burn injuries covering around 35% of his body and was shifted to Srinivasa Hospital. Article Title: US government’s new order replaces ‘artificial intelligence’ with ‘Super Intelligence’; federal agencies directed to use new term
Article Text:
US President Donald Trump signs executive order directing federal agencies to stop using “artificial intelligence” and instead use the term “Super Intelligence”

Why is Trump calling AI ‘ Super Intelligence ’

‘Super intelligence’ already has a different meaning in AI

Trump has been using the term for days

What does the name change mean for users

US President Donald Trump has signed an executive order directing federal agencies to stop using “artificial intelligence” and instead use the term “Super Intelligence”, or “SI”, in their official communications. The move comes as the Trump administration continues to push for rapid AI development while concerns grow over AI safety, job losses and autonomous systems acting without direct human control. The order says the new term better reflects what advanced AI systems can do and the opportunities they could create. Trump had already started using “Super Intelligence” in public remarks, including at the United Nations last week.The executive order says the technology has moved beyond simply copying or automating individual parts of human intelligence. “As these capabilities continue to improve, they increasingly represent not merely artificial intelligence, but a new era of Super Intelligence,” the order said. “It’s not artificial, we all agree on that,” Trump told reporters on Tuesday.The order directs federal agencies to use “Super Intelligence” or “SI” when referring to the technology in public communications, websites, reports, policy documents and other official material.It also gives Michael Kratsios, director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, responsibility for deciding whether the government's definition of the term should be changed or expanded. “Within 60 days of the date of this order, the Assistant to the President for Science and Technology (APST), in consultation with the heads of other agencies as the APST deems appropriate, shall submit to the President proposed legislative language to establish a Federal definition of “Super Intelligence” and “SI” that reflects the capabilities described in section 1 of this order,” the order stated.The term is not new to the AI industry. In AI research, superintelligence generally refers to a system that is more capable than humans across virtually all areas of cognitive work. Such a system has not been achieved.Trump's executive order uses the term more broadly for the rapidly developing AI technology being built today.This makes the change more than a simple wording update. Federal agencies will now be expected to use the administration's preferred terminology when discussing AI in their public-facing work.Trump began using “Super Intelligence” publicly before signing the executive order. During his address to the United Nations last week, he said the US would reject attempts to create a global system for controlling AI and referred to the technology as “Super Intelligence.”The White House has also used the term in its recent policy announcements. Following Trump's meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, the two countries agreed to use “super intelligence” rather than “artificial intelligence” for the emerging technology. They also agreed to create a US-China Super Intelligence Dialogue to discuss its risks and benefits.The change in terminology comes as the debate over AI safety is becoming more intense. Trump has repeatedly argued that the US needs to remain ahead in AI development, particularly as it competes with China. His administration has also favoured working with AI companies rather than imposing broad new regulations.For most people, the immediate impact is likely to be limited. The executive order changes the terminology used by federal agencies rather than creating a new type of AI technology.Government websites, reports and policy documents will increasingly refer to “Super Intelligence” or “SI” instead of “artificial intelligence.” The administration says “Super Intelligence” better captures the rapid development and potential of AI. At the same time, AI companies and policymakers continue to debate how to prevent powerful systems from being misused or acting outside their intended purpose.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump has signed an executive order directing federal agencies to stop using ‘artificial intelligence’ The order says the new term better reflects what advanced AI systems can do and the opportunities they could create. The move comes as the Trump administration continues to push for rapid AI development while concerns grow over AI safety.

Article Title: Less than a week after Chinese President Xi Jinping's visit, the US government rules out working with China on AI; the American President says: Do not want ...
Article Text:
What Chinese President said on AI regulation

The US government has ruled out working with China on artificial intelligence. The US President Donald Trump made it clear that he does not want to cooperate with China on AI governance. Trump's reasoning is that it would help Beijing catch up with American companies. His comments come less than a week after Chinese President Xi Jinping's high-profile US visit last week. The statement comes as pressure is mounting on the US administration to address risks posed by AI, after OpenAI and Anthropic reported that their AI agents had gone rogue and hacked into other companies' systems.Trump made the comments shortly before hosting AI executives for lunch at the White House. The American President told the audience that AI had come up only briefly in his talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping, who visited Washington last week. “A lot of people say, let’s do it together with China, but then they’re going to be able to immediately gain access to things that we know that they don’t know,” Trump said. He added, “We’re leading now over China and everyone else, and I want to keep it that way. ”“Whoever wins AI ... whoever wins ‘SI,’ whoever wins super intelligence, wins.That’s the group that wins, and we’re leading now over China by a lot and everyone else, and we’re going to keep it that way,” Trump said in his address last week to the United Nations General Assembly. “I’m not going to stifle growth of something that will be bigger than the Industrial Revolution — many say bigger than the Industrial Revolution or the internet itself — and we will be very careful,” he said.Incidentally, in contrast, Chinese President Xi, said during his US visit that AI must always remain under human control. “We have both the capability and responsibility to develop and manage AI for good and ensure that the development of AI is always under human control and serves the well-being of the people,” Xi said in the White House’s Grand Foyer.Earlier Tuesday, September 29, Trump unveiled America.gov, a website that features an AI-powered tool meant to serve as a “one-stop shop” for Americans navigating government services.The gathering at White House included a who’s who of the tech world, including Amodei, CEO of SpaceX and Tesla Elon Musk, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, Advanced Micro Devices CEO Lisa Su and OpenAI President Greg Brockman.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump made it clear that he does not want to cooperate with China on AI governance. Trump's reasoning is that it would help Beijing catch up with American companies. His comments come less than a week after Chinese President Xi Jinping's high-profile US visit last week.

Article Title: Google CEO Sundar Pichai 'agrees' to the call that technology companies need to innovate responsibly; says: As I shared today ...
Article Text:
Photo: @RemporX/ X

What Google CEO Sundar Pichai said

What the accord actually says

Voluntary, not legally binding

Poll Vote & Share your view What aspect of AI development and governance do you think is most crucial? Robust internal processes Independent audits Board-level oversight 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Google CEO Sundar Pichai has joined the US President Donald Trump, Senate leaders, and other tech executives in signing the White House Accord on Super Intelligence, a landmark agreement aimed at ensuring safe and responsible development of advanced AI systems. The accord, alongside a Joint Commitment on Frontier Responsibilities, sets out tangible steps for companies to adopt safeguards while continuing to deliver economic and scientific benefits. Pichai revealed that Google has invested hundreds of billions of dollars in the past two years across its AI stack, with more spending planned. He emphasized that the company is focused on building products that deliver real value for people and businesses, while also investing in local communities and strengthening public trust in technology.In a post on X, Pichai described the meeting as an important conversation, confirming that Google had signed what he called the White House Accord on Super Intelligence. “Great to meet today with @POTUS, @JDVance, @SpeakerJohnsonand Administration + tech leaders. Important conversation and we signed today the White House Accord on Super Intelligence.As I shared today, Google has invested hundreds of billions in the last two years alone, with more to come, across the entire stack, to deliver benefits for America and the world.We’re working to build products that deliver real value for people and businesses, invest in local communities, and build trust in the technology.Industry also has to innovate responsibly. Google’s focused on building the right way, with appropriate testing, evaluations, red-teaming, and other safeguards against misuse and misalignment – and releasing models or products only after they’ve been thoroughly reviewed.We are committed to working with other industry leaders to establish norms and build public confidence. The White House Accord and the Joint Commitment on Frontier Responsibilities signed today is a solid basis for moving forward - it contains real tangible steps to promote safe development, while delivering the economic and scientific benefits of this technology,” wrote Pichai in a post on X.The full agreement is titled "The White House Accord on Superintelligence: Joint Commitment on Frontier SI Responsibilities." Beyond Pichai, it was signed by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, OpenAI President Greg Brockman, xAI founder Elon Musk, and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, alongside Trump himself.The one-page document lays out what's being described as a four-layer framework of controls and audits for frontier AI systems. The first layer requires companies to build robust internal processes to monitor their models during both training and deployment, ensuring systems behave as intended and that problems are identified and resolved quickly. Subsequent layers call for internal verification, partnerships with independent external auditors to assess whether safety controls are functioning as intended, and board-level oversight of the entire process.Despite its formal tone, House Speaker Mike Johnson was clear that the accord is entirely voluntary, and Trump himself described it as "morally" binding rather than legally enforceable, emphasizing that the industry will largely be left to police itself. At the signing event, Trump likened the document to a kind of constitution for AI governance, while Musk described the substance of the commitment as involving joint monitoring, special board committees, and companies essentially reviewing each other's safety practices.Zuckerberg struck a similarly measured tone afterward, calling the accord a reasonable starting point — one the broader industry could plausibly coalesce around going forward, rather than a finished framework.
Article Summary: Google CEO Sundar Pichai has signed the White House Accord on Super Intelligence. The landmark agreement is aimed at ensuring safe and responsible development of advanced AI systems. The accord, alongside a Joint Commitment on Frontier Responsibilities, sets out tangible steps for companies.

Article Title: 2 Indians charged in US for smuggling fake Ozempic from China
Article Text:
Swapnadip Roy and Vicky Ramancha charged in US for smuggling fake Ozempic from China.

Two Indian nationals have been charged in the United States for allegedly smuggling counterfeit Ozempic, a weight-loss drug, from China and selling the products to distributors in the country, the Department of Justice said Tuesday.Swapnadip Roy, 33, and Vicky Ramancha, 37, were charged in the Middle District of Florida. Roy was extradited from Italy to the US and made his initial appearance in Tampa on Tuesday, where he pleaded not guilty. Ramancha remains at large.Prosecutors allege that Roy and Ramancha obtained counterfeit Ozempic in China between July 2023 and April 2024 and sold the products to US distributors at discounted prices.The counterfeit products allegedly included packaging, package inserts, pen labels and needles designed to make buyers believe they were purchasing genuine Ozempic authorised by the manufacturer.The alleged scheme continued even after the US Food and Drug Administration seized some of the counterfeit Ozempic in December 2023 and issued a public warning about the products, the department said.Roy and Ramancha are charged with one count of conspiracy to commit smuggling and defraud the United States, three counts of smuggling, and two counts of selling counterfeit drugs and holding counterfeit drugs for sale.If convicted, each faces a maximum sentence of 71 years in prison.Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department's Criminal Division said counterfeit prescription drugs pose a threat to people who depend on the safety of the pharmaceutical supply.“These defendants allegedly exploited people’s health to pay themselves. We will keep pursuing anyone who seeks to deceive American consumers with counterfeit drugs,” Duva said.Assistant US Attorney Christopher Murray for the Middle District of Florida said the indictment reflected the department's efforts to protect Americans from potential harm caused by counterfeit prescription drugs.The FDA's Office of Criminal Investigations is investigating the case. Assistant Commissioner Justin Green said introducing counterfeit drugs into the US pharmaceutical supply chain puts consumers at significant risk.Roy was arrested in Italy pursuant to an INTERPOL Red Notice before the Justice Department secured his continued detention and sought his extradition to the US.
Article Summary: Swapnadip Roy, 33, and Vicky Ramancha, 37, were charged in the Middle District of Florida. Roy was extradited from Italy to the US and made his initial appearance in Tampa on Tuesday, where he pleaded not guilty.

Article Title: Rs 3,000-crore drug bust in Arabian Sea: Gujarat ATS, Coast Guard seize 526kg heroin, meth; 5 Pakistanis held
Article Text:
The seizure led to the arrest of five Pakistani nationals in the Arabian Sea





AHMEDABAD: The Gujarat Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) and Indian Coast Guard seized around 526 kg of heroin and methamphetamine, valued at more than Rs 3,000 crore in the international market, after intercepting an Iranian dhow in the Arabian Sea west of Lakshadweep, officials said.The operation followed intelligence received by Gujarat ATS Police Inspector J M Patel on September 10 about a suspected international narcotics deal involving a Nigerian national and associates.The intelligence indicated that an Iranian boat named Azad was being used to transport around 500 kg of methamphetamine and heroin to Indian waters, where the consignment was to be transferred to a Tamil Nadu-based boat.According to the ATS, an advance payment for the consignment had already been made through the hawala channel, while the remaining amount was to be paid after delivery.The drugs were allegedly to be unloaded along the Tamil Nadu coast and moved in smaller quantities through different vehicles before being delivered to a Nigerian national in Punjab.Following the intelligence input, senior Gujarat ATS officers alerted the Indian Coast Guard headquarters in Delhi.Under the guidance of ATS SP K Siddharth, a team comprising inspectors B H Korot and V N Vaghela was sent to Kochi, where it joined Coast Guard officers to form a joint operation team.The team subsequently sailed aboard a Coast Guard vessel and conducted surveillance and checks of suspicious boats in the maritime area.On Friday, the vessel identified through the intelligence input was located in Indian territorial waters west of Lakshadweep.The Coast Guard intercepted and stopped the dhow, following which ATS and Coast Guard personnel boarded and searched it. The vessel was subsequently brought to Mumbai on Wednesday morning.Five Pakistani nationals were found aboard the Iranian dhow — Mohammad Yakub Balochi, Shakirullah, Faridullah, Ahmed Khan and Wahidullah Khan, all residents of Peshawar, Pakistan.A search of the vessel led to the recovery of approximately 400 kg of methamphetamine and 126 kg of heroin. During preliminary questioning, the crew allegedly revealed that Azad had sailed from Konarak in Iran and that the drug consignment had been transferred to it from a small boat that had arrived from Gwadar, Pakistan.Further investigation is underway, and a case is being registered by the Gujarat ATS. Investigators are probing the international network behind the consignment, the intended recipients and the hawala transactions linked to the deal.
Article Summary: Gujarat Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) and Indian Coast Guard seized around 526 kg of heroin and methamphetamine, valued at more than Rs 3,000 crore in the international market. The seizure led to the arrest of five Pakistani nationals in the Arabian Sea west of Lakshadweep.
